topic.title: How Do Bacteria Communicate?
topic.learning_objective: Understand how bacteria use chemical signals to communicate and coordinate behavior.

hook.narration: Bacteria don’t just live alone—they talk.

sections.narration: They use chemical signals called quorum sensing to know when they’re in a crowd. These molecules act as messages between bacteria.
Bacteria release these chemicals into their environment. When enough are present, it signals that the group is large and active.
They use this signal to form protective biofilms or switch from harmless to harmful states. It’s a way to work together as a team.
This communication shapes their behavior and survival. Scientists study it to develop new ways to fight infections and improve health.

closing.narration: Bacteria use chemical signals to talk, cooperate, and survive—key insights that drive breakthroughs in science and medicine.

full_narration:
Bacteria don’t just live alone—they talk.

They use chemical signals called quorum sensing to know when they’re in a crowd. These molecules act as messages between bacteria.

Bacteria release these chemicals into their environment. When enough are present, it signals that the group is large and active.

They use this signal to form protective biofilms or switch from harmless to harmful states. It’s a way to work together as a team.

This communication shapes their behavior and survival. Scientists study it to develop new ways to fight infections and improve health.

Bacteria use chemical signals to talk, cooperate, and survive—key insights that drive breakthroughs in science and medicine.
